facts.text: Slimebot-volleyball is a 3D version of slime volleyball, implemented on top of slimevolleygym and using Webots as a simulator for visualization
The README calls the project a gym-like environment and says gym must be installed
The README says the same physics as slimevolleygym is used, so the environment can run in a CMD without Webots
The Webots Supervisor import is optional: outside Webots the import fails and WEBOTS_MODE is False
The game settings are TIMESTEP = 1/30 s, NUDGE = 0.1, FRICTION = 1.0, INIT_DELAY_FRAMES = 30, GRAVITY = -9.8*2*1.5 and MAXLIVES = 5
The non-pixel action space is spaces.MultiBinary(5) and the observation space is a Box with 18 values bounded by +-np.finfo(np.float32).max
An episode is done when t reaches t_limit or when either agent's life is <= 0
The observation is [agent x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, ball x, y, z, vx, vy, vz, opponent x, y, z, vx, vy, vz] divided by 10.0
Action values 0 to 4 select forward, backward, jump, right and left when they are greater than 0
The caller's action controls agent_right and the baseline policy controls agent_left unless otherAction is supplied
Game.reset starts the ball at x=0, y=width/4-1.5, z=0 with vx uniform in [-20, 20], vy uniform in [10, 25] and vz uniform in [-10, 10]; the agents start at -width/4 and width/4 at height 1.5
A ball at the floor scores for the opposite side: checkEdges returns -1 when x <= 0 and 1 otherwise, and the game negates that for the right agent's reward
The README lists the observation shape as 18 for 1 vs 1 and 30 for 2 vs 2
TeamVolleyBot uses the same MultiBinary(5) action space and a Box observation with 30 values

determinism.notes: reset(seed) reseeds the fake's Python random generator and its dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake uses Python's random.Random and a simplified collision model while the clone uses numpy's generator and its own physics, so one seed does not give the same trajectory as the clone

gaps: reduced physics: the fake models gravity, the five binary actions, wall bounces and the floor-contact score, but not the curved fence, agent/ball collision impulses, friction, the delay screen or the baseline policy's motion
the fake uses Python's random.Random(seed) and returns Python float lists; the clone uses numpy's generator and numpy float arrays, so a seed does not reproduce the clone's trajectory
the baseline opponent is static on the left half instead of BaselinePolicy; the observation order and the /10.0 scaling follow RelativeState.getObservation
reset options are accepted by the family bridge but have no effect in the fake
no rendering, no Webots Supervisor, no pixel observations and no 2-vs-2 TeamVolleyBot (30 values)
the fake was not compared with an upstream run: the gate environment has no gym, opencv or Webots module (numpy is present, but the clone also needs gym), and only the family contract is checked
the episode ends at t_limit 3000 or when a side loses 5 lives; scoring and lives are reduced to the floor-contact rule

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
